c.tagline: Okanagan wine country on a sun-soaked lake, ringed by vineyards, beaches, and ski slopes.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around C$3.50 plus per-km charges. Kelowna Cabs and the local Current Taxi app operate citywide; Uber and Lyft also serve Kelowna and are often cheaper.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada; 811 (HealthLink BC) is the non-emergency health advice line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Some street disorder around the Leon Avenue area downtown late at night.

hood_desc: The walkable core along Bernard Avenue and the Okanagan Lake waterfront, packed with restaurants, breweries, City Park beach, the marina, and the Kelowna Art Gallery; the best base for first-time visitors who want to be in the middle of everything.

A relaxed lakeside village just south of downtown with cafes, boutiques, the Pandosy Waterfront Park, and Gyro Beach; suits travelers who want beach access and a local, low-key vibe within reach of the centre.
A leafy, upscale residential area stretching along the lake south of Pandosy, home to sandy beaches, parks, and easy access to Mission-area wineries; good for families and a quiet, resort-style stay.
Kelowna's craft-brewery and light-industrial district north of downtown below Knox Mountain, with tasting rooms, indie eateries, and hiking trails; suits younger travelers and beer-and-outdoors fans.

A more affordable, diverse residential hub east of the centre with big-box shopping, international restaurants, and quick highway access to the airport and Big White ski resort; good for budget-conscious travelers with a car.
lodging: Delta Hotels by Marriott Grand Okanagan Resort
Hotel Eldorado, an Autograph Collection Hotel
Best Western Plus Kelowna Hotel & Suites

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00am to 11:00pm on most routes, with reduced service on evenings, weekends, and holidays; there is no rapid transit, so ride-hail or a car fills late-night gaps.
transit.note: Kelowna has no rail, metro, or tram; the BC Transit bus network (including frequent routes along Highway 97 and to UBC Okanagan) is the only public transit, and a car is the easiest way to reach lakeside wineries, beaches, and Big White ski resort.
transit.pay: Pay cash on board (exact fare, about C$2.50) or tap the reloadable Umo card or Umo mobile app that BC Transit uses in Kelowna. A DayPASS is about C$5, and single-ride transfers are valid for connecting buses.

bus: BC Transit Kelowna Regional Transit System
Ebus / FlixBus (intercity to Vancouver, Kamloops, Vernon)

transit.m: BC Transit Route 23 Airport toward downtown / UBCO (~40-50 min)
